title: Leverage Dynamics in Product-Market Networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.02960v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We examine whether corporate leverage persistence reflects only firms' own adjustment frictions or also the past financing choices of economically connected firms. We combine annual firm fundamentals with time-varying text-based product-market networks and estimate a heterogeneous dynamic partial-adjustment model with interactive effects using defactored instrumental variables. The estimator accommodates time- varying network weights and spatial dependence in firm-specific coefficients. Network-weighted lagged leverage is positive and statistically significant, with a mean coefficient representing approximately 45% of the sum of the own and network lag coefficients for book leverage. Accounting for network dependence reduces the persistence attributed to firms' own financing histories and increases the implied own-firm speed of adjustment. translated_title: 产品市场网络中的杠杆动态
translated_abstract: 我们检验企业杠杆的持续性是仅反映了企业自身的调整摩擦，还是也受到经济关联企业过去融资选择的影响。我们将年度企业基本面数据与时变的基于文本的产品市场网络相结合，使用去因子工具变量估计了一个具有交互效应的异质性动态部分调整模型。该估计方法能够处理时变的网络权重以及企业特定系数中的空间依赖性。网络加权的滞后杠杆系数为正且在统计上显著，其平均系数约相当于账面杠杆的自滞后系数与网络滞后系数之和的45%。在考虑网络依赖性之后，归因于企业自身融资历史的持续性有所降低，而企业自身隐含的调整速度有所提高。企业特定估计结果揭示了自有杠杆持续性中存在显著的产品市场聚集现象。
tldr: 该论文将基于文本的时变产品市场网络引入异质性动态部分调整模型，发现企业杠杆持续性中约45%来自经济关联企业的过去融资选择，揭示了企业杠杆决策存在显著的网络传染效应。
en_tdlr: This paper incorporates time-varying text-based product-market networks into a heterogeneous dynamic partial-adjustment model, finding that roughly 45% of corporate leverage persistence stems from the past financing choices of economically connected firms, revealing significant network spillover effects in leverage decisions.
